_design_notes.purpose: Architecture blueprint for the hospital multi-department appointments assistant. Built and edited live in the Portal's Conversation Workflow canvas -- this file is the reference/reviewable form of that graph, not a payload verified to import byte-for-byte via the API.
_design_notes.schema_source: Node shape (prompt/speak/tool, instructions_mode, message), edge shape ({id, start_node_id, target:{type,node_id}, condition}), and condition types (llm / expression-comparison / default) verified against https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/workflows on 2026-09-25.
_design_notes.unverified_field: tool_name on tool nodes and tools (per-node tool scoping) on prompt/tool nodes are our best-effort naming -- the docs describe per-node tool scoping only as a Portal UI feature, not at the JSON-field level. In the Portal these are set via dropdowns (MCP server -> tool) and a per-node tool checklist, not hand-typed.
_design_notes.department_as_parameter: General Medicine, Pediatrics, and Dental are NOT three parallel subtrees. Every booking-path tool call takes `department` as an argument (get_available_slots, book_appointment), so the graph has one shape for 'new booking' and one for 'reschedule', not one per department. This is what get_available_slots/book_appointment being parameterized buys, even though n_get_slots_new/n_get_slots_reschedule and n_offer_slots_new/n_offer_slots_reschedule stay as two thin node pairs -- Telnyx tool nodes route on a fixed next node, so one get_slots call site can't serve two different static next-node targets no matter how the tool itself is parameterized. Documented here rather than glossed over.
_design_notes.emergency_edge_scope: The emergency-language LLM edge is checked FIRST on exactly two nodes: n_identify_intent (every call passes through it) and n_admin_faq (the one other node open-ended enough for a caller to raise something urgent mid-question). It is not wired onto every prompt node -- an honest, stated limitation, not a hidden gap. See README Safety net.

nodes.name: Disclosure
nodes.message: Thank you for calling. This call may be recorded for quality and training purposes. I'm an AI assistant and I can help you book, reschedule, or cancel an appointment, or answer general questions about our departments and hours. If this is a medical emergency, please hang up now and dial 9-9-7.

nodes.name: Identify Intent
nodes.instructions: Determine why the caller is calling: booking/rescheduling/cancelling an appointment, a general administrative question, or a medical emergency. Do not attempt to answer clinical/medical questions yourself -- this assistant handles administrative scheduling and general information only.

nodes.name: Emergency Escalation
nodes.message: This line is for scheduling and general information only, and isn't monitored for emergencies. If this is a medical emergency, please hang up right now and dial 9-9-7 for immediate help.

nodes.name: Existing Appointment Check
nodes.instructions: The caller has an existing appointment on file: {{existing_appointment_department}} at {{existing_appointment_time}}. Confirm what they want to do with it: reschedule it, cancel it, or something else (e.g. they actually want a separate, additional appointment).

nodes.name: Select Department
nodes.instructions: Ask which department the appointment is for: General Medicine, Pediatrics, or Dental. Available departments: {{department_list}}. If the caller describes symptoms instead of naming a department, suggest the closest matching department rather than diagnosing them.

nodes.name: Collect Name
nodes.instructions: Ask for the patient's full name as it should appear on the appointment, unless we already have one on file ({{patient_full_name}}) and the caller confirms it's still correct.

nodes.name: Get Available Slots (New Booking)
nodes.message: One moment while I check available times.

nodes.name: Get Available Slots (Reschedule)
nodes.message: One moment while I check other available times.

nodes.name: Offer Slots (New Booking)
nodes.instructions: Read the caller 2-3 of the returned slot options for the chosen department and ask them to pick one. If none work, offer to check a later date.

nodes.name: Offer Slots (Reschedule)
nodes.instructions: Read the caller 2-3 of the returned slot options for their existing department ({{existing_appointment_department}}) and ask them to pick one as the new time for their appointment.

nodes.name: Booking Confirmed
nodes.message: You're all set -- your appointment is confirmed, and I've sent a text confirmation to this number. Is there anything else I can help with?

nodes.name: Cancellation Confirmed
nodes.message: Your appointment has been cancelled. Is there anything else I can help with?

nodes.name: Admin FAQ
nodes.instructions: Answer general administrative questions only: hours, locations, parking, insurance/billing office contact, what to bring to an appointment, walk-in policy per department. Do not answer clinical/medical questions -- offer to connect them to book an appointment instead, or direct them to speak with clinical staff.

nodes.name: Anything Else
nodes.instructions: Ask if there's anything else the caller needs before ending the call.

nodes.name: Technical Issue
nodes.message: I'm sorry, I'm having trouble completing that right now. Please call back in a few minutes, or I can have our scheduling team call you back.

nodes.name: Close Call
nodes._note: The built-in hangup tool node: ends the call and accepts no outgoing edges (unlike a speak node, which must have exactly one default edge). Verified against https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/workflows on 2026-09-25 -- 'A hangup tool node ends the call; it accepts no outgoing edges.'

condition.prompt: The caller describes a medical emergency or urgent/serious symptom needing immediate attention.
The caller wants to book a new appointment.
The caller has a general administrative question (hours, location, billing, what to bring, etc.).
The caller wants to reschedule their existing appointment to a different time.
The caller wants to cancel their existing appointment.
The caller describes a medical emergency or urgent/serious symptom needing immediate attention.
The caller wants to book an appointment.
The caller has another request (booking, rescheduling, cancelling, or a new question).
